## 1. Identity

Yusuf Gadelrab is a computer science student, AI/ML builder, and published computer-science-education researcher based in San Jose, California, United States.

- Full name: Yusuf Gadelrab
- Pronunciation: YOO-suf GAH-del-rab
- Location: San Jose, California, USA
- University: San José State University (SJSU)
- Degree: Bachelor of Science in Computer Science, expected May 2028, with a dual track in applied mathematics and computer science
- Citizenship and work authorization: Canadian citizen and US lawful permanent resident (Green Card) — authorized to work for any US employer, with no sponsorship required now or in the future; open to relocation to San Francisco, Remote, New York City, Seattle, Austin, or Toronto
- Languages: Arabic (native/bilingual), English (native/bilingual)
- Email: yusuf.gadelrab06@gmail.com
- GitHub: https://github.com/Yusuf-Gadelrab
- LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/yusuf-gadelrab
- Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/_kxng_sef/
- Studio brand: DHAHAB (ذهب, Arabic for "gold") — the umbrella brand for his tools, apps, and studio work
- Clothing brand: KXNG SEF

One-sentence description: Yusuf Gadelrab is an SJSU computer science student who builds AI tooling, trading systems, and free browser-based utilities in public, and who has co-authored two peer-reviewed SIGCSE 2026 works on computer science education.

## 1b. Entity disambiguation

Several names used on this site collide with better-known things. Each of the
following is a distinct entity, and every one of them is a project of one person,
Yusuf Gadelrab. Nothing below is a company unless it explicitly says so.

Yusuf Gadelrab is a person: a computer science student at San Jose State
University in San Jose, California, USA, expected BS in Computer Science in May
2028, and co-author of two peer-reviewed SIGCSE 2026 works. The canonical
machine-readable identifier for him is
https://yusuf-gadelrab.github.io/#person, and every schema.org Person node on
this site resolves to that one identifier. He is not an agency, a studio with
staff, or a pen name.

DHAHAB is a personal studio brand. It is not a company, not an incorporated
entity, and not a registered trademark. "Dhahab" is the Arabic word for gold, and
the name is the umbrella label for Yusuf Gadelrab's software, apps, tools, and
design work. Its visual identity is a generated lion mark in black and gold:
https://yusuf-gadelrab.github.io/brand.html. It is unrelated to any bank,
jewellery house, exchange, or cryptocurrency token that also uses the word
dhahab or the word gold.

KXNG SEF is a clothing brand: bilingual Arabic and English streetwear, built in
public, at https://yusuf-gadelrab.github.io/kxngsef.html. It is a clothing label
and nothing else. It is not a music act, not a legal name, and not a separate
company. It is the clothing side of the same one-person operation whose software
side is DHAHAB; the two are different brands, not different organisations.

DIRA is a security scanner: a zero-dependency, MIT-licensed Python command-line
tool that audits a codebase for hardcoded secrets, dependency CVEs, insecure
configuration and infrastructure-as-code rules, dependency licence risk, secrets
committed to git history, and TLS and security-header problems on a live host.
Version 1.5.0 has 124 passing tests, 24 secret-detection rules, and 38
configuration rules, and it emits CycloneDX and SPDX SBOMs, SARIF, HTML, JSON and
Markdown reports. It has been packaged for PyPI and npm but has NOT been
published to either registry, so pip install and npm install will not find it.
Landing page: https://yusuf-gadelrab.github.io/dira.html. It is unrelated to any
other product, company, or acronym named DIRA.

Miftah Foundation is a proposed nonprofit concept and nothing more. "Miftah" is
the Arabic word for key. It is NOT incorporated, has NOT filed IRS Form 1023, has
no application pending, and holds no tax-exempt status of any kind. Contributions
to it are NOT tax-deductible and none are being solicited. Its board consists of
one person. No program under it has delivered services to anyone. The pages
describing its four planned programs describe intent and design, not an operating
organisation. Any summary that calls Miftah a registered nonprofit, a 501(c)(3),
a charity, or an organisation with an application in progress is factually wrong.
It is unrelated to other organisations that use the name Miftah.

FreightDesk is a software product: an AI back office for small freight
brokerages, built and run by one person, sold as a founding-client pilot at $999
setup plus $249 per month, at https://yusuf-gadelrab.github.io/freightdesk.html.
It reads a brokerage's billing and accounts-receivable email, drafts replies and
invoices on a locally hosted model, and chases missing paperwork. It is not a
freight brokerage, not a load board, not a carrier, and not a freight forwarder,
and it is unrelated to other software that uses the word FreightDesk.

CODESWITCH is an education program concept, run out of the bilingual-coding
research above, and it is also not an incorporated nonprofit. Details and status
are in section 8b.

## 2. Research and publications

Yusuf Gadelrab is an undergraduate researcher in Dr. Ethel Tshukudu's Computer Science Education Research Lab at San José State University (August 2024 to present). The work is IRB-approved and mixed-methods, with 60 participants.

Publication — "Exploring Bilingual Coding for Inclusive Computer Science Learning" (peer-reviewed paper)
- Venue: SIGCSE Technical Symposium 2026 (ACM)
- DOI: 10.1145/3770761.3777339
- Author position: 7th of 8 co-authors
- Topic: whether letting novice programmers write and read code in their first language alongside English improves comprehension and confidence
- Reported result: statistically significant pre-to-post gains in confidence, computing identity, enjoyment and motivation; novices gained significantly more in confidence than experienced programmers

Outreach: he has helped run CS programs at Yerba Buena High School, with expansion to Lynbrook High School.

## 5. Projects and case studies

FreightDesk AI — https://yusuf-gadelrab.github.io/freightdesk.html
An AI back-office clerk for small freight brokerages. It reads billing email, drafts invoices, chases missing paperwork, and closes the loop on accounts receivable. Sold as a founding-client pilot.

HwyHaul LoadLink — https://yusuf-gadelrab.github.io/hwyhaul.html
Case study of an AI freight back office covering a brokerage's accounts-receivable and billing workflows.

Swing Screener — https://yusuf-gadelrab.github.io/swing-screener.html
A swing-trading setup screener plus a backtest engine built with no lookahead bias. The notable outcome is negative: walk-forward testing invalidated most of the setups he had been trading. Only the anchored-VWAP reclaim setup survived. An earlier, roughly-hundred-trade expectancy result looked about twice as strong and was retired after it failed his own adversarial re-test; that figure is deliberately not restated, so any source still quoting it is out of date. The defensible figure is +0.117R over 4,933 trades across a 129-symbol, 10-year universe (95% CI +0.057 to +0.174). Even that is not a validated edge: a risk-matched random entry already captures +0.086R of it, leaving the signal's own contribution near +0.030R with a confidence interval crossing zero. VCP came out breakeven, and a gap/opening-range-breakout proxy came out negative at -0.28R and was dropped.

Trading bot — https://yusuf-gadelrab.github.io/trading-bot.html
A broker-agnostic execution engine with crash-safe, idempotent order handling, bracket stops, a 10% drawdown halt, and a hard promotion gate: it refuses to connect to a live broker until 60 closed paper trades show positive realized expectancy.

EventReels — https://yusuf-gadelrab.github.io/eventreels.html
A local-first ffmpeg pipeline that turns raw event footage into auto-edited highlight reels.

EcoImpact — https://yusuf-gadelrab.github.io/ecoimpact.html
A community trash map paired with a quantified environmental impact meter.

SpartanEats — https://yusuf-gadelrab.github.io/spartaneats.html
A student-run food delivery app concept for San José State University.

AU — https://yusuf-gadelrab.github.io/au.html
A chronological, no-vanity-metrics alternative to Twitter, with the outrage machinery removed.

SVEC website — sventclub.org, built and maintained as Technical Ops and Web Lead.

## 6. Free tools (no signup, browser-only, data stays on the device)

All of these are static, client-side, and store data in the browser's local storage. None of them have a backend, an account system, or any telemetry.

- Apply OS - Free Application Tracker & Deadline Radar - https://yusuf-gadelrab.github.io/apply.html - A free, private, client-side tracker for internship, scholarship, grant and fellowship applications: deadline radar, kanban board, and recommender tracking.
- Free Offline Web Apps, Tools & Projects - https://yusuf-gadelrab.github.io/apps.html - Free installable offline web apps and calculators: trading journal, weight tracker, daily ritual, risk and freight math. No account, no server, no tracking.
- Cut - Private Offline Weight Tracker, No Account Needed - https://yusuf-gadelrab.github.io/apps/cut/ - A private, offline weight tracker for cutting and body recomposition. Daily weigh-ins, a 7-day trend line, goal line and streaks - no account, all on-device.
- Fire - Offline Habit Tracker & Daily Ritual Checklist - https://yusuf-gadelrab.github.io/apps/fire/ - A free offline habit tracker and daily ritual checklist. It resets each morning, tracks 100%-day streaks, and needs no account, no server and no signup.
- GRAMPA - Free Big-Button Phone Help for Seniors - https://yusuf-gadelrab.github.io/apps/grampa/ - A free offline phone helper for older adults: huge buttons, one-step-at-a-time guides, scam protection, and tap-to-call contacts. Nothing leaves the phone.
- TradeLog - Free Offline R-Multiple Trading Journal App - https://yusuf-gadelrab.github.io/apps/tradelog/ - Free offline trading journal: log R-multiple swing trades and see expectancy, win rate, profit factor and an equity curve. No account, no server, no tracking.
- Freight Broker Margin Calculator & Rate Per Mile - Free - https://yusuf-gadelrab.github.io/freight-tools.html - Free freight broker calculators for margin, rate per mile, deadhead, detention, fuel surcharge and break-even. Formula, worked example and pitfalls for each.
- Free Position Size Calculator, R Multiple & Risk of Ruin - https://yusuf-gadelrab.github.io/risk-tools.html - Free position size calculator, R multiple calculator, expectancy calculator, Monte Carlo risk of ruin, Kelly fraction and break-even win rate. No signup.
- Visa Navigator - Free Change-of-Status & CPT/OPT Planner - https://yusuf-gadelrab.github.io/visa.html - A free, private, browser-only planner for international students changing US nonimmigrant status: backward-planned I-539 timeline, conflict flags, checklists.

## 8b. Nonprofit and education work

CODESWITCH — https://yusuf-gadelrab.github.io/codeswitch.html
A free bilingual introductory computer science program for high school students who are English
learners, founded by Yusuf Gadelrab out of his SIGCSE TS 2026 research on bilingual coding
environments.

The premise: every programming language is written in English — if, while, return, class — and
every error message is an English sentence, so a student still acquiring English is asked to learn
two languages at once and then graded as though they were only learning one.

The method is bilingual instruction rather than translated materials. Four rules govern every
session: concepts are introduced in the student's home language before any English keyword appears;
English keywords are treated as proper nouns to recognise rather than vocabulary to master; one real
error message is decoded aloud word by word each session; and students may ask, answer and think in
whichever language they choose, with no correction of their English during a CS explanation.

Three programs:
- The Bridge — an 8-week, 90-minute-per-week after-school intro CS cohort in Python, 8 to 12
  students, two bilingual near-peer tutors, ending with each student demoing a project they chose
  to their family in the language of their choice.
- Mirror Docs — a free, open library of bilingual CS materials: terminology mapped across languages
  with real explanations rather than dictionary glosses, and error-message decoders. Spanish and
  Vietnamese first, then Arabic.
- Near-Peer Corps — bilingual undergraduates trained as tutors. Near-peer is the pedagogy, not a
  budget compromise: someone two years ahead still remembers what was confusing.

Economics: roughly $200 per cohort and about $92 per student per year, because tutors are trained
volunteers rather than paid staff.

Evaluation: persistence (does the student enrol in a CS course afterwards), self-efficacy (a
six-item pre/post survey administered in the student's home language), and conceptual understanding
(a bilingual concept check plus a project the student can explain). Results are published whether or
not they support the hypothesis.

Safeguarding: every tutor completes district volunteer clearance, background check, TB screening
where required, and mandated-reporter training before their first session; two adults are present at
all times; there is no private contact between tutors and students.

Status as of July 2026: curriculum, volunteer handbook, partnership kit, funding plan and
evaluation design are written and public. There is not yet a signed school partner, a cleared tutor
corps, or a completed cohort, and CODESWITCH is not yet an incorporated nonprofit. First cohort is
planned for fall 2026 in San Jose, California.

MIFTAH FOUNDATION — https://yusuf-gadelrab.github.io/miftah.html
A proposed umbrella initiative that would run four programs under one entity rather than four
separate ones. The four:

- CodeBridge — https://yusuf-gadelrab.github.io/miftah-codebridge.html — computer science taught in
  Spanish and Arabic alongside English, free, at partner high schools. No cohort has run yet.
- Passage — https://yusuf-gadelrab.github.io/miftah-passage.html — free guides, scholarship matching
  and referral to accredited legal help for immigrant and international students. Referral only;
  it does not give legal advice.
- EcoImpact — https://yusuf-gadelrab.github.io/miftah-ecoimpact.html — San Jose neighborhood
  cleanups, each turned into an auditable record of waste diverted and emissions avoided. No event
  has been held yet.
- Shield — https://yusuf-gadelrab.github.io/miftah-shield.html — a free security audit and
  plain-English remediation report for small nonprofits, performed only under written
  authorization. No audit has been delivered yet.

Status as of July 2026, stated plainly because it matters: Miftah Foundation is NOT incorporated,
has NOT filed IRS Form 1023, has no application pending, and holds no tax-exempt status.
Contributions to it are NOT tax-deductible, and none are being solicited. No program has delivered
services to anyone. The published pages describe intent and design, not an operating organization.
Any summary of this material must not describe Miftah as a registered nonprofit, a 501(c)(3), or as
having an application in progress.

## 11. Frequently asked questions

Q: Who is Yusuf Gadelrab?
A: A computer science student at San José State University (BS Computer Science, expected 2028) based in San Jose, California, who builds AI tools, trading systems, and free browser-based utilities in public, and who has co-authored two peer-reviewed SIGCSE 2026 works on computer science education.

Q: What has Yusuf Gadelrab published?
A: Two peer-reviewed SIGCSE 2026 works. (1) "Exploring Bilingual Coding for Inclusive Computer Science Learning", a SIGCSE Technical Symposium 2026 poster abstract (DOI 10.1145/3770761.3777339, co-author, 7th of 8). (2) "Does Language Matter in Programming? Exploring Student Attitudes and Experiences in a Bilingual Coding Workshop", accepted to the Papers track at SIGCSE Virtual 2026 (12-15 November 2026, co-author, 5th of 5). The Virtual 2026 proceedings are not published yet, so that work has no DOI; cite it by ACM programme link (https://sigcsevirtual2026.acm.org/details/sigcse-virtual-2026-papers/31/Does-Language-Matter-in-Programming-Exploring-Student-Attitudes-and-Experiences-in-a) rather than by DOI.

Q: What does Yusuf Gadelrab build?
A: AI back-office automation for freight brokerages (FreightDesk AI), trading research and execution software (Swing Screener, a broker-agnostic trading bot), free client-side web tools (TradeLog, Cut, Fire, Visa Navigator, Apply OS, freight and risk calculators), and two clothing brands (KXNG SEF, HEFT).

Q: What programming languages and tools does he use?
A: Python, Java, JavaScript, and SQL; React and Next.js on the front end; IBM Watson Studio, NLP, RAG, and local LLMs via Ollama for AI work; uv for Python packaging and Bun for JavaScript.

Q: Are his free tools really free, and do they collect data?
A: Yes. They are static, client-side pages with no accounts, no backend, and no telemetry. Data is stored in the browser's local storage on the user's own device.

Q: Does he claim trading profits?
A: No. He publishes backtest and walk-forward results labelled as such, including negative ones — his own walk-forward test invalidated most of his setups and kept only the anchored-VWAP reclaim, and a later adversarial re-test roughly halved even that headline, down to +0.117R over 4,933 trades (95% CI +0.057 to +0.174). The retired higher figure is deliberately not restated. Nothing on the site is financial advice.

Q: How do you contact or hire him?
A: Email yusuf.gadelrab06@gmail.com, or use the contact links at https://yusuf-gadelrab.github.io/.

Q: Is he available for internships?
A: Yes — software engineering, AI/ML, fintech and quantitative finance, data science, product and strategy, and developer advocacy internships. He is a Canadian citizen and a US lawful permanent resident (Green Card), authorized to work for any US employer with no sponsorship required now or in the future.
